messages.author: 262bfcbf6d4ecc3a
messages.subject: log x and y bug?
parts:
Has anyone tried to generate graphs logging the X and Y axes using a
loess smooth? I can log the Y and plot just fine, but the X gives me
warnings like...

1: pseudoinverse used at 0.68857
2: neighborhood radius 0.69773
3: reciprocal condition number 5.2738e-16
4: There are other near singularities as well. 0.1644
5: In predLoess(object$y, object$x, newx, object$s, object
$weights, ... :
pseudoinverse used at 0.68857

The range of X values is 1:5.

The Y values run from about 200 to 1000

I can post my code but my dataset is very large.

p <- ggplot(s, aes(day, log(rt), linetype = endo))
p <- p + stat_smooth(method = 'loess')
p <- p + facet_wrap(~subj)
p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(5.6,6.5))
p

messages.author: 262bfcbf6d4ecc3a
messages.subject: Re: log x and y bug?
parts:
It turns out that the subject of the post is misleading. If I log the
values, (1,2,3,4,5) first and just use the already transformed data
for my X-axes the problem persists. Perhaps it's just certain
floating point numbers? Ah, and there we have part of it, if I just
take day (the X-value) and divide it by 3 I don't get the problem.
And it's not the fact that I have a 0 in there (log(1)) because
subtracting 1 doesn't cause the problem either. So far, the only
special set of floating point values that won't work is the log of my
X values.

(I'd much rather use the axis scaling syntax but that also fails with
similar errors)

It isn't floating point, it isn't anything but a log transform (any
base). It's a limited kind of error.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: log x and y bug?
parts:
It's a mystery:

# Manually fit the loess models so we can figure out exactly
# where the error is occuring
options(warn = 2)
smoothes <- dlply(s, c("subj", "endo"), function(df) {
loess(log(rt) ~ log(day), data = df)
}, .inform = T)
options(warn = 0)

# Problem is (at least) with subj BW & endo i
# So let's look at in more detail

prob <- subset(s, subj == "BW" & endo == "i")
qplot(day, rt, data = prob)
qplot(log(day), log(rt), data = prob)

qplot(log(day), log(rt), data = prob) + geom_smooth()

# I don't know what's the problem. The only think I
# can think of it's some numeric problem due to the discreteness
# of the x

qplot(jitter(log(day)), log(rt), data = prob) + geom_smooth()
